passages.text: This is what the Lord GOD showed me: I saw a basket of summer fruit.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD is the one who rules over all.
The Lord GOD showed me something.
I saw a basket.
The basket held summer fruit.
passages.original: כֹּ֥ה הִרְאַ֖נִי אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה וְהִנֵּ֖ה כְּל֥וּב קָֽיִץ׃

passages.text: “Amos, what do you see?” He asked. “A basket of summer fruit,” I replied. So the LORD said to me, “The end has come for My people Israel; I will no longer spare them.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord spoke to Amos.
The Lord asked Amos a question.
The Lord said, “Amos, what do you see?”
Amos answered the Lord.
Amos said, “I see a basket of summer fruit.”
The Lord spoke to Amos again.
The Lord said, “The end has come for My people Israel.”
The Lord said, “I will not spare them any longer.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מָֽה־ אַתָּ֤ה רֹאֶה֙ עָמ֔וֹס וָאֹמַ֖ר כְּל֣וּב קָ֑יִץ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י בָּ֤א הַקֵּץ֙ אֶל־ עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹא־ אוֹסִ֥יף ע֖וֹד עֲב֥וֹר לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: “In that day,” declares the Lord GOD, “the songs of the temple will turn to wailing. Many will be the corpses, strewn in silence everywhere!”
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He says, “In that day, the songs in the temple will become wailing.
There will be many dead bodies.
Corpses will lie everywhere.
People will throw them down in silence.”
passages.original: וְהֵילִ֜ילוּ שִׁיר֤וֹת הֵיכָל֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה רַ֣ב הַפֶּ֔גֶר בְּכָל־ מָק֖וֹם הִשְׁלִ֥יךְ הָֽס׃פ

passages.text: Hear this, you who trample the needy, who do away with the poor of the land, asking, “When will the New Moon be over, that we may sell grain? When will the Sabbath end, that we may market wheat? Let us reduce the ephah and increase the shekel; let us cheat with dishonest scales.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to those who oppress the needy.
You trample the poor of the land.
You ask, “When will the New Moon be over?”
You want to sell grain.
You ask, “When will the Sabbath end?”
You want to market wheat.
You say, “Let us reduce the ephah.”
You want to give less product.
You say, “Let us increase the shekel.”
You want to charge more money.
You say, “Let us cheat with dishonest scales.”
You plan to deceive and steal.
passages.original: שִׁמְעוּ־ זֹ֕את הַשֹּׁאֲפִ֖ים אֶבְי֑וֹן וְלַשְׁבִּ֖ית עַנְוֵי אָֽרֶץ׃ לֵאמֹ֗ר מָתַ֞י יַעֲבֹ֤ר הַחֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ וְנַשְׁבִּ֣ירָה שֶּׁ֔בֶר וְהַשַּׁבָּ֖ת וְנִפְתְּחָה־ בָּ֑ר לְהַקְטִ֤ין אֵיפָה֙ וּלְהַגְדִּ֣יל שֶׁ֔קֶל וּלְעַוֵּ֖ת מֹאזְנֵ֥י מִרְמָֽה׃

passages.text: Let us buy the poor with silver and the needy for a pair of sandals, selling even the chaff with the wheat!”
passages.sermon:
The people are greedy and corrupt.
\r\nThey want to buy the poor for silver.
\r\nThey want to buy the needy for a pair of sandals.
\r\nThey sell even the chaff mixed with the wheat.
\r\nThey treat people as things to be bought and sold.
\r\nThey cheat others for their own gain.
passages.original: לִקְנ֤וֹת בַּכֶּ֙סֶף֙ דַּלִּ֔ים וְאֶבְי֖וֹן בַּעֲב֣וּר נַעֲלָ֑יִם וּמַפַּ֥ל בַּ֖ר נַשְׁבִּֽיר׃

passages.text: The LORD has sworn by the Pride of Jacob: “I will never forget any of their deeds.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD is holy and powerful.
The LORD has sworn an oath.
The LORD swears by the Pride of Jacob.
The LORD says, “I will never forget their deeds.”
The LORD will remember everything they have done.
The LORD will not forget their actions forever.
passages.original: נִשְׁבַּ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה בִּגְא֣וֹן יַעֲקֹ֑ב אִם־ אֶשְׁכַּ֥ח לָנֶ֖צַח כָּל־ מַעֲשֵׂיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Will not the land quake for this, and all its dwellers mourn? All of it will swell like the Nile; it will surge and then subside like the Nile in Egypt.
passages.sermon:
God sees the evil deeds of the people.
The land will shake because of these deeds.
Everyone who lives in the land will mourn.
The whole land will rise up like the Nile River.
The land will be tossed about and sink down again.
This will happen just as the Nile in Egypt rises and falls.
passages.original: הַ֤עַל זֹאת֙ לֹֽא־ תִרְגַּ֣ז הָאָ֔רֶץ וְאָבַ֖ל כָּל־ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בָּ֑הּ וְעָלְתָ֤ה כָאֹר֙ כֻּלָּ֔הּ וְנִגְרְשָׁ֥ה וְנִשְׁקָה כִּיא֥וֹר מִצְרָֽיִם׃ס

passages.text: And in that day, declares the Lord GOD, I will make the sun go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the daytime.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He says what will happen in that day.
The Lord GOD will act with power.
He will make the sun go down at noon.
He will darken the earth during the day.
Light will turn to darkness at a time when it should be bright.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֣ה׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְהֵבֵאתִ֥י הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ בַּֽצָּהֳרָ֑יִם וְהַחֲשַׁכְתִּ֥י לָאָ֖רֶץ בְּי֥וֹם אֽוֹר׃

passages.text: I will turn your feasts into mourning and all your songs into lamentation. I will cause everyone to wear sackcloth and every head to be shaved. I will make it like a time of mourning for an only son, and its outcome like a bitter day.
passages.sermon:
The Lord God speaks.
He will change your feasts into mourning.
He will turn all your songs into lamentation.
He will make everyone wear sackcloth around their waist.
He will cause every head to be shaved.
He will make this time like mourning for an only son.
The end will be like a bitter day.
passages.original: וְהָפַכְתִּ֨י חַגֵּיכֶ֜ם לְאֵ֗בֶל וְכָל־ שִֽׁירֵיכֶם֙ לְקִינָ֔ה וְהַעֲלֵיתִ֤י עַל־ כָּל־ מָתְנַ֙יִם֙ שָׂ֔ק וְעַל־ כָּל־ רֹ֖אשׁ קָרְחָ֑ה וְשַׂמְתִּ֙יהָ֙ כְּאֵ֣בֶל יָחִ֔יד וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖הּ כְּי֥וֹם מָֽר׃

passages.text: Behold, the days are coming, declares the Lord GOD, when I will send a famine on the land— not a famine of bread or a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the words of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He is the ruler of all.
He says, “Days are coming.”
I will send a famine on the land.
This famine will not be for bread.
This famine will not be for water.
This famine will be for hearing the words of the LORD.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֣ה׀ יָמִ֣ים בָּאִ֗ים נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְהִשְׁלַחְתִּ֥י רָעָ֖ב בָּאָ֑רֶץ לֹֽא־ רָעָ֤ב לַלֶּ֙חֶם֙ וְלֹֽא־ צָמָ֣א לַמַּ֔יִם כִּ֣י אִם־ לִשְׁמֹ֔עַ אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: People will stagger from sea to sea and roam from north to east, seeking the word of the LORD, but they will not find it.
passages.sermon:
People will move from one sea to another sea.
They will travel from the north to the east.
They will wander everywhere.
They will look for the word of the LORD.
They will not find the word of the LORD.
passages.original: וְנָעוּ֙ מִיָּ֣ם עַד־ יָ֔ם וּמִצָּפ֖וֹן וְעַד־ מִזְרָ֑ח יְשֽׁוֹטְט֛וּ לְבַקֵּ֥שׁ אֶת־ דְּבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א יִמְצָֽאוּ׃

passages.text: In that day the lovely young women— the young men as well— will faint from thirst.
passages.sermon:
God is speaking about a coming time of judgment.
God will send a famine of hearing His words.
People will search for God's word but will not find it.
In that day, beautiful young women will faint from thirst.
Young men will also faint from thirst.
passages.original: בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא תִּ֠תְעַלַּפְנָה הַבְּתוּלֹ֧ת הַיָּפ֛וֹת וְהַבַּחוּרִ֖ים בַּצָּמָֽא׃

passages.text: Those who swear by the guilt of Samaria and say, ‘As surely as your god lives, O Dan,’ or, ‘As surely as the way of Beersheba lives’— they will fall, never to rise again.”
passages.sermon:
Some people swear by the guilt of Samaria.
These people say, “As surely as your god lives, O Dan.”
They also say, “As surely as the way of Beersheba lives.”
These people will fall.
They will never rise again.
passages.original: הַנִּשְׁבָּעִים֙ בְּאַשְׁמַ֣ת שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן וְאָמְר֗וּ חֵ֤י אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ דָּ֔ן וְחֵ֖י דֶּ֣רֶךְ בְּאֵֽר־ שָׁ֑בַע וְנָפְל֖וּ וְלֹא־ יָק֥וּמוּ עֽוֹד׃ס
